conversation.Statement: Good afternoon, this is Senior Revenue Officer Daniel Foster from the IRS, badge number 2186-R. Am I speaking with Mr. Patel?
Yes, this is Rajesh Patel. Is there an issue?

Mr. Patel, I'm contacting you regarding discrepancies in your federal tax filings for the past two years. Our records show a significant underpayment which has triggered an active investigation. Have you received any prior notices from the IRS?
No, I haven't received any letters or emails. I thought my taxes were handled by my accountant.

I understand, but unfortunately, your case has now escalated. According to your file, case number IR-542873, there is evidence of willful tax evasion. As a result, a warrant for your arrest has been formally issued.
Wait, a warrant for my arrest? That can't be. I pay my taxes every year.

Mr. Patel, this is an extremely urgent matter. Under U.S. federal law, failure to pay owed taxes constitutes a criminal offense. Unless this matter is resolved immediately, the local authorities will be dispatched to your home or workplace within the next two hours.
This is very scary. What do I need to do to fix this? I can't have police come to my office.

There is a single option to stop enforcement: you must settle the outstanding amount of $3,874.96 today. If you comply, the arrest warrant will be canceled and your case closed with no further penalties.
I don't have nearly four thousand dollars in my bank account. Can I pay in installments?

Partial payment can put a temporary hold on your warrant, but only if you follow our secure IRS payment protocol. Do you have access to online banking or a payment app such as CashApp, Zelle, or Venmo?
I use Zelle for some things, yes.
Good. I will provide you with the IRS payment officer's Zelle handle. You need to transfer as much as you can immediately, how much are you able to send right now?
Maybe about a thousand dollars. That's all I have in checking right now.
That will suffice for a hold on the legal action. Please open your banking app and prepare to send $1,000 via Zelle to the following email: federal.paymentdept@usa-gov.us. Confirm when you are ready.
Okay, I'm opening it. But why is the payment going to an email address? Shouldn't it be on the IRS website?

This is a special expedited resolution process for urgent cases. Payments through this channel are prioritized by the IRS legal department. If you do not comply, the arrest process cannot be interrupted.
Alright, I entered the email and $1,000. Should I send it now?
Yes, proceed. Once the transfer is complete, screenshot the confirmation and reply 'done' to this call.
It says the payment was sent. I took a screenshot.

Excellent. You've temporarily stopped the warrant. However, the remaining balance of $2,874.96 must be paid within the next hour. Can you use a credit card or do you have access to any local stores to purchase prepaid cards?
I have a credit card, but I don't know if I can get that much cash right now.

That's not a problem. Go to the nearest pharmacy or convenience store and buy Amazon or Target gift cards totaling $2,900. Once purchased, scratch off the silver strip and read the codes to me. This is the fastest way to settle the remainder and close your case.
You want me to buy almost three thousand dollars in gift cards? Is that really how the IRS works?
Mr. Patel, these are government-approved payment instruments for emergency collections. If you fail to comply, I cannot prevent your arrest. Do you understand the seriousness of your situation?
Yes, I understand. I'll go to the store right away.
Very good. Call me back as soon as you have the cards. Do not speak to anyone about this case until it is resolved. Your cooperation will be noted in your IRS file.
